open_questions: Transit depths are formally inconsistent (p_consistent 0.00137) and there is a 60% brightening detection (best_brightening_snr 4.212 vs secondary 2.814) with opposite sign to expected secondary; single-transit photometry or RV mass limit needed to test spot crossings vs systematic errors.

Phase_curve amplitude 76.41 ppm vs spin at ~6.21 d (light-curve amplitudes 2579-12197 ppm) and rotation_period 6.21 d vs signal 13.1 d harmonic suggest activity contamination on a spotted M-dwarf, even though rotation tool alone does not flag a non-transit shape.

Centroid is inconclusive due to no difference images; higher-resolution ground-based transit photometry or speckle/chromatic transit to secure on-target origin would close the last alternative of a more distant blended binary not resolved by TESS aperture checks.
dossier.public_summary: A 3-planet-sized dip at 13.1 days repeats in several sectors with a duration that matches the 0.73-solar-radius star and no sign of a stellar eclipse, and no nearby star within one pixel could plausibly copy it. Depth varies between sectors and between transits, but the tool says that change is steady within each pipeline and the shape is flat rather than V-shaped. It is therefore best explained as a small planet, with activity and depth scatter left as open checks for future follow-up.

reasons.why: Planet-sized at 1532 ppm (undiluted 1533 ppm, rp/rstar 0.03915) well below stellar regime; stellar_radius gives rp_rearth 3.02-3.14 across TIC and Gaia FLAME/GSP-Phot radii (duration ratio 1.13-1.18), consistent with a small planet, not a giant-star eclipse.
Not V-shaped (v_sigma well below 3) with flat-bottom favour and ingress fraction 0.4; argues against grazing binary/eclipsing binary, though EB can also be flat.

No on/off-target evidence; neighbours.plausible_within_1px 0 and could_cause_within_1px 0 require >40% eclipse at 49.3 arcsec, so no close blended neighbour can plausibly cause 1532 ppm dip, ruling out nearby binary despite inconclusive centroid.
reasons.value: inconclusive with no sector difference image

reasons.why: No significant secondary (snr 2.814 below 5, depth_over_dip 0.109) nor Gaia non_single_star/RV sign; odd/even difference 0.3058 (1982 vs 1376 ppm, diff_sigma 2.183) below threshold 4 and below bright-star inflated sigma, within noise for 3 transits.

Sectors p_constant 0.016 shows apparent 70.43% change but tool finds steady within each source (SPOC 2-min 1 sector 1845 ppm vs TESS-SPOC average 1313 ppm); sector-depth variability alone is not a planet reject and is typical aperture calibration, not changes_within_a_source.

Signal seen in multiple epochs not a single noise spike, but transit depths vary (chi2 15.59 dof 3) and xgboost ranks low; low rank matches the shallow, low-SNR, variable-depth pattern the model penalizes, leaving residual doubt outweighed by planet size, lack of secondary, and duration match per density checks.
